mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of these triggers at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both above 12-month moving average simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, inflation expectations rise despite low rates, eroding real equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 5% significance.
